Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries

  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
IMPORTANT: WebFetch WILL FAIL for authenticated or private URLs. Before using this tool, check if the URL points to an authenticated service (e.g. Google Docs, Confluence, Jira, GitHub). If so, look for a specialized MCP tool that provides authenticated access.

- Fetches content from a specified URL and processes it using an AI model
- Takes a URL and a prompt as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts HTML to markdown
- Processes the content with the prompt using a small, fast model
- Returns the model's response about the content
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: If an MCP-provided web fetch tool is available, prefer using that tool instead of this one, as it may have fewer restrictions.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - localhost and other hostnames without a dot are not supported; for a local server, use curl via Bash
  - The prompt should describe what information you want to extract from the page
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large
  - Includes a self-cleaning cache (entries expire after 15 minutes) for faster responses when repeatedly accessing the same URL
  - When a URL redirects to a different host, the tool will inform you and provide the redirect URL in a special format. You should then make a new WebFetch request with the redirect URL to fetch the content.
  - For GitHub URLs, prefer using the gh CLI via Bash instead (e.g., gh pr view, gh issue view, gh api).

本项目由“tanqf”开发。

# Orphan-Interface Scan — Edge/Embedded C++ (branch dev/feature, READ-ONLY)

Scope scanned: `server/src/**`, `server/include/**`, `client/**`, `tools/**`, `scripts/**` (non-harness), `config.yaml`, all `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/`, 12 `.bpf.c` programs, root entrypoints (`init.sh`, `start_platform.sh`), `.docker/`. No file was modified.

---

## FINDINGS (by severity)

### Important-1 — Polling observation D-Bus methods (15) + C-API wrappers (19): test-only callers
- **Surface**: D-Bus methods `ListInterfaces`, `GetInterfaces`, `Ping`, `GetBluetoothDevices`, `GetBluetoothAdapter`, `GetBluetoothAudioQuality`, `GetCoexistenceConflict`, `GetDnsStats`, `GetWifiLossStats`, `GetHttpLatencyStats`, `GetProcessProfiling`, `GetSkbDropStats`, `GetTcpRttStats`, `GetEbpfMonitorHealth`, `GetHistory` — dispatch table `server/src/dbus_service.cpp:94-211`; handlers at `dbus_service.cpp:378, 689, 802, 852, 890, 977, 1067, 1105, 1144, 1182, 1229, 1280, 1348, 1455`. Matching C API in `client/weaknet_client.h` (shipped: `libweaknet.so` installed by `tools/ci.sh:143`).
- **Evidence**: per-function sweep over `client server tools scripts` (`*.cpp/*.c/*.sh`, excluding `client/client.cpp`): all 19 wrappers (`weaknet_health_check`, `weaknet_get_interfaces`, `weaknet_ping_host`, `weaknet_get_bluetooth_{devices,adapter,audio_quality}`, `weaknet_subscribe_event`, `weaknet_subscribe_bluetooth_events`, `weaknet_subscribe_network_quality`, `weaknet_get_{dns,wifi_loss,http_latency_stats,process_profiling,skb_drop_stats,tcp_rtt_stats,ebpf_monitor_health,coexistence_conflict,history}`, `weaknet_check_changes`) are called only from `client/test_client.cpp`, `client/example_usage.cpp`, `client/ping_example.cpp`, `client/test_network_quality.cpp` — test harness or binaries excluded from packaging (`tools/ci.sh:129` target list). `client/weaknet_cli.cpp` (the shipped ops CLI) contains **0** `weaknet_subscribe*` calls and no stats commands; `tools/weaknet-test-full.sh` drives only `test-client`; no cloud/edge exporter performs D-Bus calls (exporters read monitors/SQLite directly).
- **Classification**: test-only caller. Verified production code (shipped via ci.sh; the other 15 methods — config family, `GetDiagnosis`, `ExecuteAction`, `GetNetworkExperience`, `Query*`, `HealthCheck` — do have real consumers in weaknet-cli / `client/weaknet-offline-diag`).
- **Severity**: Important. **Consequence**: ~half the advertised public API surface (README "C/C++ 客户端二次集成") is maintained, versioned and shipped with zero representative production consumer; any drift in these 15 methods is invisible to every real consumer.
- **Disposition**: **replan with a real consumer** — either expose a thin `weaknet-cli stats`-style consumer for the subset worth keeping, or shrink the shipped D-Bus/C-API surface to the consumed subset.

### Important-2 — All 7 D-Bus signals: dispatched in production, zero production subscribers
- **Surface**: `Changed`, `InterfaceChanged`, `ConnectionModeChanged`, `NetworkQualityChanged`, `BluetoothDeviceChanged`, `MonitorStateChanged`, `EbpfMonitorStats` — `server/include/common.hpp:65-72`. Emitters: `server/src/event_manager.cpp:114-127`, `server/src/server.cpp:184, 840, 1443`, `server/src/dbus_service.cpp:234, 309, 637, 677`, `server/src/bt_monitor.cpp:1516`.
- **Evidence**: subscribers only via `client/client.cpp:588-593` match registration inside `weaknet_subscribe_*`, whose callers (per sweep above) are test/example binaries only; `grep -c weaknet_subscribe client/weaknet_cli.cpp` = 0; no other in-repo subscriber. Notably `server/src/server.cpp:1062-1064` comments the eBPF stats signal "替代轮询 Get*Stats" — the replacement subscriber was never built.
- **Classification**: dead dispatch (emitted, never subscribed by any production consumer). `kSignalSerializedFile` (`common.hpp:107`) is *not* part of this — it is local-file persistence with a real consumer at `client/client.cpp:311` (cleared).
- **Severity**: Important. **Consequence**: an entire async integration contract (and the "signals replace polling" design claim) ships without a single production listener; the claim in code comments is currently false.
- **Disposition**: **replan with a real consumer** (e.g. `weaknet-cli stats --watch` subscribing to `EbpfMonitorStats`), or stop emitting until a consumer exists.

### Important-3 — `tcp_retrans` and `tcp_conn` eBPF pipelines: probes live, data consumed by nothing in production
- **Surface**: plugins `TcpRetransPlugin`/`TcpConnPlugin` (`server/src/monitor_ebpf_plugins.cpp:227-298`), probes `server/src/tcp_retransmit.bpf.c`, `server/src/tcp_conn_stats.bpf.c`; worker threads `server/src/server.cpp:1048-1072` (tcp_retrans: LOG + `emitEbpfStats("tcp_retrans")` at 1064) and `server/src/server.cpp:1074-1094` (tcp_conn: LOG only). Both `enabled: true` in `config.yaml`.
- **Evidence**: non-test references to `tcp_retrans_monitor`/`tcp_conn_monitor` are only lifecycle wiring (`monitor_ebpf_plugins.cpp:242-254, 286-298`), context pointers (`server/include/server.hpp:113, 253-254`), and the health registry (`dbus_service.cpp:1377-1378`, consumed only via test-only `GetEbpfMonitorHealth`). Data-path absence proved by: no `GetTcpRetransStats` method exists in the 30-method dispatch; neither monitor appears in the SLE block (`server.cpp:417-551`); absent from `server/src/edge_wireless_uplink_exporter.cpp` and `server/src/edge_telemetry_exporter.cpp` (grep `tcp_retrans|tcp_conn` → no hits); absent from `handleGetDiagnosis` which reads only `assessment_store.latest()` (`dbus_service.cpp:490-493`); absent from history persistence (no history file in the full `grep -rl tcp_retrans server/src` file list). The only eBPF-stats signal subscriber set is empty (Finding 2), so the tcp_retrans signal is also unconsumed. tcp_conn's `getStats()` is consumed nowhere outside its own thread (`grep 'tcp_conn_monitor->'` → only registry static_cast).
- **Classification**: attached-but-never-producing-consumed-output (production). Note the contrast: `tcp_connect`, `tcp_rtt`, `http_latency`, `skb_drop`, `process_profiler`, `dns`, `wifi_loss` all have real production sinks (SLE evaluators / metrics registry / wireless uplink).
- **Severity**: Important. **Consequence**: two always-on kernel probe pipelines burn CPU/memory on a small ARM board while README:14-15 advertises them as core diagnostic features whose data never reaches any decision, persistence or export path.
- **Disposition**: **replan with a real consumer** — wire their aggregates into history persistence / diagnosis facts / uplink, or default-disable them.

### Important-4 — `tools/verify_v1_contract.sh`: self-declared mandatory gate that nothing ever runs
- **Surface**: `tools/verify_v1_contract.sh` (header self-describes as mandatory v1 contract gate, checks C1-C4; internally invokes `tools/dns-assurance-acceptance.sh`).
- **Evidence**: `grep -rln 'verify_v1_contract' .` (repo-wide, excluding `.git`) → **only the script itself**. Not referenced by `tools/ci.sh`, `.github/workflows/*`, any `scripts/*.sh`, README or docs. `dns-assurance-acceptance.sh` is separately referenced (the script itself + docs), so the underlying acceptance tooling is alive; only this wrapper/gate is unreachable.
- **Classification**: no-caller entrypoint (never-wired gate / superseded entrypoint).
- **Severity**: Important. **Consequence**: a guarantee the repo believes is enforced (v1 contract gate C1-C4) is silently never executed — false safety signal.
- **Disposition**: **remove** the wrapper (keep `dns-assurance-acceptance.sh`, which is the documented, reachable piece).

### Important-5 — README quickstart 方式一 references `start_platform.sh` from the wrong cwd — command cannot work as written
- **Surface**: `README.md:199-203` — `cd Large-Model-Application` then `./start_platform.sh`.
- **Evidence**: `find . -name 'start_platform.sh' -not -path './.git/*'` → only `./start_platform.sh` at repo root; the script itself `cd`s into the LMA dir internally (`start_platform.sh:53`), i.e. it is designed to run from the repo root. After the README's `cd`, `./start_platform.sh` does not exist. (方式二 `./scripts/dev_lite.sh` *does* exist inside LMA, so the two methods contradict each other's cwd requirements.)
- **Classification**: unreachable-artifact as documented / contradictory entrypoint.
- **Severity**: Important. **Consequence**: the primary documented command for standing up the cloud platform fails immediately for any new user.
- **Disposition**: **replan** the instruction to match reality: run `./start_platform.sh` from the repo root (it handles the LMA cd itself).

### Minor-6 — Legacy audio cluster: `a2dp_media` / `bt_audio_fusion` / `GetBluetoothAudioQuality` — documented default-off, but no exit condition
- **Surface**: `server/src/bpf/a2dp_media.bpf.c` (only loaded when `bluetooth.a2dp_fusion_enabled=true`); fusion block `server/src/server.cpp:762-800` gated by `bt_monitor.cpp:1427` (comment at 1453: "superseded by bt_hci_traffic"); D-Bus `handleGetBluetoothAudioQuality` `dbus_service.cpp:890`; C API `weaknet_get_bluetooth_audio_quality` (test-only, Finding 1).
- **Evidence**: default `false` in code (`server/src/weaknet_config.cpp` serialize at 1291; key absent from `config.yaml`); with default config the fusion path returns early, and `handleGetBluetoothAudioQuality` returns an error JSON when transports are empty. Production consumers: none. Documentation claim verified true: `README.md:167` ("旧 A2DP 音频探针默认停用") and `docs/产品定位-工业无线诊断网关.md:35,173-174` mark it legacy/optional.
- **Classification**: test-only caller + parsed-but-runtime-gated legacy (documented).
- **Severity**: Minor. **Consequence**: dead-by-default code paths and one D-Bus method linger with no removal criterion.
- **Disposition**: **document as intentional incubation with exit condition** — README already documents default-off; add an explicit exit condition (remove after the `bt_hci_traffic` replacement is confirmed on-board for N releases).

### Minor-7 — `TcpConnectMonitor::consumeLostEvents` and `getCaptureDiagnostics`: dead public API
- **Surface**: `server/src/tcp_connect_monitor.cpp:387-392` (`consumeLostEvents`, drains `impl_->lost_events` written at 208 by `on_tcp_lost`) and `:394` (`getCaptureDiagnostics`); declarations `server/include/tcp_connect_monitor.hpp:102, 105`.
- **Evidence**: unfiltered whole-repo grep `consumeLostEvents|getCaptureDiagnostics` (`--include=*.cpp/*.hpp/*.h`): the only hits are these definitions/declarations plus `dns_monitor`'s *own* equivalents — whose callers *do* exist (`dns_monitor.cpp:678`, `server.cpp:877`). No caller of the TcpConnectMonitor versions anywhere, including tests. Note the monitor itself is alive (SLE consumes `recentObservations()`/`stats()` at `server.cpp:447-451`); only these two methods are dead — `impl_->lost_events` is written but only ever read by the uncalled `consumeLostEvents` (the live loss counter is the separate `drain_stats.lost_events` reported via `stats()`).
- **Classification**: no caller (internal cross-file API never used).
- **Severity**: Minor. **Consequence**: misleading API symmetry with DnsMonitor implies consumption that doesn't exist; a silently-accumulating dead counter.
- **Disposition**: **remove** both methods and the dead `impl_->lost_events` counter.

### Minor-8 — `tools/bt_hci_probe_test.bpf.c`: compiled by nothing, referenced by nothing
- **Surface**: `tools/bt_hci_probe_test.bpf.c`.
- **Evidence**: `grep -rln 'bt_hci_probe_test' .` → only itself. Not in any `CMakeLists.txt`, not built by `tools/ci.sh`, not referenced by any script, workflow, test or doc. (The production BT data-path probe is `server/src/bpf/bt_hci_traffic.bpf.c`, fully wired via `BtHciTrafficPlugin` → DB + L2 anomaly detector.)
- **Classification**: unreachable-artifact.
- **Severity**: Minor. **Consequence**: stray kernel-probe source in `tools/` that will silently rot (vmlinux/layout drift) and confuses readers about which BT probe is real.
- **Disposition**: **remove**.

### Minor-9 — Root `init.sh`: zero-reference entrypoint superseded by documented workflows
- **Surface**: `./init.sh` — body is `scripts/openspec_preflight.sh; scripts/context_reset_check.sh; scripts/resume_from_snapshot.sh`.
- **Evidence**: `grep -rn '\binit\.sh\b' . --include=*.md/*.sh/*.yml` (excluding `.git`, excluding `dev_lite` matches) → **no hits**. Not referenced by README, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/ai/*, CI, or any script.
- **Classification**: superseded-entrypoint / no caller.
- **Severity**: Minor. **Consequence**: a third workflow bootstrap path exists beside the documented harness commands, with no caller to keep it in sync if the three harness scripts change.
- **Disposition**: **remove** (the OpenSpec docs already prescribe the real entry commands).

### Minor-10 — Client example/test binaries built by default, never shipped or invoked by automation
- **Surface**: CMake targets `example_usage`, `ping_example`, `test_network_quality` (`client/CMakeLists.txt:35-49`) and `test_lifecycle_api` (`:24-25`, also `add_test` at `:53`).
- **Evidence**: absent from the ci.sh packaging target list (`tools/ci.sh:129`: `weaknet-dbus-server history_query_tool weaknet weaknet_cli test_client_bin test_ebpf ebpf`) and from all install lines; repo-wide invocation sites: none (only `docs/架构设计-模块与代码结构.md:110-111` lists the filenames as directory inventory). `test_lifecycle_api` is at least consumed by x86 ctest; the other three are never executed by any automation and are the sole non-test callers behind the test-only C-API cluster of Finding 1 (`weaknet_ping_host`, `weaknet_subscribe_event`, `weaknet_subscribe_network_quality`).
- **Classification**: unreachable-artifact (shipped=no).
- **Severity**: Minor. **Consequence**: default builds compile three never-run binaries; they blur the line between test fixtures and public examples.
- **Disposition**: **document as intentional** C-API usage examples/ctest fixtures (they mirror the README integration sample), keeping them excluded from `dist-arm64`.

### Minor-11 — `AI-assisted analysis/` blanket "DEPRECATED" claim is false for two live production files
- **Surface**: `AI-assisted analysis/README.md:3` declares the whole directory a deprecated RAG prototype; but `AI-assisted analysis/edge_network_rag.py` and `AI-assisted analysis/network_knowledge_base.py` are live production artifacts.
- **Evidence**: shipped by `tools/ci.sh:144-145` into `dist-arm64/`; executed by `server/src/assurance/edge_ai_scheduler.cpp` (default `script_path = "/home/radxa/weaknet/edge_network_rag.py"`, `server/include/assurance/edge_ai_scheduler.hpp:59`) and by `client/weaknet_cli.cpp:288-319` (`diagnosis --ai` popen with fallback candidates). The remaining 12 `.py` prototypes in the directory have no references and match the DEPRECATED claim.
- **Classification**: doc-vs-code inconsistency in a known-legacy area (the 12 dead prototypes themselves are correctly documented).
- **Severity**: Minor. **Consequence**: a reader following the directory README would delete or stop shipping two files that the board-side AI scheduler and weaknet-cli actively require.
- **Disposition**: **document** — correct the directory README to name the two live shipped scripts and their consumers; keep DEPRECATED for the other 12.

---

## Scope covered / candidates checked and cleared

- **eBPF programs (12 .bpf.c, all inventoried)**: `dns_monitor`→SLE DnsServiceEvaluator+history; `wifi_packet_loss`→metrics registry (`server.cpp:937-941`); `http_latency`→SLE HttpAccessEvaluator (`server.cpp:493-498`)+signal; `flow_rate`/traffic→metrics registry; `tcp_connect`→SLE TcpConnectEvaluator (`server.cpp:447-455`); `tcp_rtt`→SLE TcpRttEvaluator (`server.cpp:472`) **and** wireless uplink (`server.cpp:1529-1535`); `skb_drop`→wireless uplink (`server.cpp:1522-1528`); `bt_events`→event store/DB/incidents; `bt_hci_traffic`→`bt_data_path_metrics` DB + L2 anomaly detector; `a2dp_media`→default-off documented legacy (Minor-6). Only `tcp_retrans`/`tcp_conn` failed (Important-3).
- **config.yaml keys**: every key has a live reader — monitor sections via `weaknet_config.cpp`+plugin init; `map_sizing_mode/entries/ram_budget_bp` verified read at every plugin init (`monitor_ebpf_plugins.cpp:60, 145, 190, 234, 278, 325-330, 422`); `portal_*`/`https_enabled`/`targets` in `active_connectivity_monitor.cpp:629-641`; `incident_*` in BT anomaly detector; `capture_pages` in Dns plugin; `stall_timeout_ms`/`min_expected_bps` etc. in `bt_data_path_anomaly_detector.cpp`; `edge.*` in both exporters.
- **Env vars**: `WEAKNET_DATA_DIR` real (`server/include/common.hpp:82` getenv + `tools/weaknet-server.service:13`); `WEAKNET_HAVE_*` are compile-time ifdefs.
- **C API**: all 42 declared functions have ≥1 caller (no zero-caller declarations); production-consumed subset verified per-function (config family, diagnosis, action, experience, events/incidents/bt-traffic → weaknet-cli).
- **D-Bus production half**: 15 methods consumed by `weaknet-cli` (`client/weaknet_cli.cpp:363-426`) and `client/weaknet-offline-diag` (shipped `tools/ci.sh:142`, uses `GetDiagnosis`+`HealthCheck` via dbus-send, documented at `docs/架构设计-模块与代码结构.md:649`).
- **history_query_tool**: invoked by `tools/ci.sh:129,137`, `.github/workflows/build-and-deploy.yml`, README:184-187, 交叉编译 docs; every queried table has a verified writer (insertSnapshot/saveDeviceBaseline/event store/incidents/insertBtDataPathMetric).
- **tools/ live or documented**: `ci.sh`, `weaknet-test-full.sh`, `weaknet-server.service`, `com.example.WeakNet.conf`, `verify_telemetry_contract.py` (root `ci.yml`), and operator/analysis tooling referenced from docs (`analyze_soak.py`, `soak_monitor.py`, `assurance-matrix.sh`, `dns-assurance-acceptance.sh`, `dns_oracle.py`, `interference_test.py`, `benchmark_models.py`, `llama-server.service`).
- **scripts/ non-harness**: `setup_arm64_sysroot.sh` (README/CLAUDE/docs/ci.sh), `setup_libcurl_sysroot.sh` (`server/CMakeLists.txt`), `setup_opensacle_sysroot.sh`→`setup_openssl_sysroot.sh` (invoked by the libcurl script + CMake), `audit_summary.sh`/`campaign.sh`/`event_audit.sh`/`quick_brief_check.sh` (docs/ai/* + harness callers).
- **.docker/arm64-builder/Dockerfile**: documented manual image build (`docs/交叉编译与开发板部署.md:175,695`); CI pulls the ghcr equivalent (`build-and-deploy.yml:36-37`) — not orphaned. (Side note, out of C++ scope: `docs/本地LLM部署方案.md` references `.docker/arm64-builder/Dockerfile.llama`, which does not exist.)
- **Other cleared**: `kSignalSerializedFile` file-persistence path; `net_traffic.cpp`'s embedded `trace_tcp_retransmit` kprobe (feeds the traffic plugin, independent of the tcp_retrans plugin); `latest_conflict_json` writer/reader pair (the D-Bus method itself is folded into Finding 1); `tools/__pycache__` not git-tracked; `weaknet_get_history` vs `history_query_tool` (production query path is the tool).
